> 「如来有肉眼不？」「如是，世尊！」……「如来有佛眼不？」「如是，世尊！」……「过去心不可得，现在心不可得，未来心不可得。」

The eighteenth section asks whether the Tathāgata has eyes, five times.

Gross flesh eyes; divine eyes that see through distance and obstruction; the eye of wisdom that sees the emptiness of all dharmas; the eye of dharma that sees the distinctions of methods and capacities; the buddha eye that holds both without falling to either side.

Five yeses, in order, from coarse to fine. Then, at the end of the section, the three minds that cannot be got.

## The five are apertures, not superpowers

The list is read in popular Buddhism as a hierarchy of psychic capacities, with 天眼 the prize and 佛眼 the summit.

The book's reading is different: these are apertures — ways the same thing is seen. 肉眼 sees surface. 天眼 sees what distance hides; it is still a vision of marks. 慧眼 sees that marks have no substance. 法眼 sees, within that emptiness, exactly how causes and capacities differ, and therefore how to teach. 佛眼 is not a sixth and better aperture: it is not being stuck in any of the previous four.

Which reframes the whole question of attainment. The path does not add a new instrument. It removes the blockage at each instrument, until nothing is being held in front of the eye.

## 天眼 is still inside the frame

The book is pointed here, because the temptation is strong: a person who can see at a distance, or see what is coming, has gained something remarkable — and remarkable things are exactly what the mind grips.

If 天眼 is an attainment, then the one who has it has acquired a mark. The section's structure says otherwise: the eye is listed as one of five that the Tathāgata possesses, not as a reward for the Tathāgata's practice. Possession is not the point; freedom from the possession is.

## 恒河沙 again

Asked whether the sand of the Ganges is sand, the Buddha says yes — sand is sand.

Small exchange, large function. After seventeen sections of cancellation, the text confirms an ordinary fact. The formula does not abolish the world; it removes the grip on it. Sand remains sand. What changes is that no one is standing on it.

## 三心不可得

The section's real turn: past mind cannot be got, present mind cannot be got, future mind cannot be got.

The misreading is that one should therefore stop thinking about past and future — that memory and planning are errors. The book refuses this. Recollection happens; planning happens; both are useful, sometimes necessary.

不可得 means not obtainable as a thing to hold. Look for the present mind: by the time you locate it, it is the past. Look for the past mind: it has already gone. The three are not hiding; they are not there in the way the searching assumes.

## What this does to the search for a self

If past, present, and future mind cannot be got, then the "I" that would own them has no location either — it is not in any of the three.

The five eyes see; the three minds cannot be found. Put together, the section is describing a perception without a perceiver standing behind it — which is what the old texts mean by 一体同观, seeing as one.

## The test

Try to find your present mind. Not describe it — find it, the way you would find a coin in a pocket.

Then notice what happened: the finding keeps turning into a description, and the description is already a moment late.

That lateness is not a failure of attention. It is the eighteenth section, delivered in person.
